title: AI data centres on federal land: policy, projects and oversight
subtitle: A source-linked timeline from January 2025 to the latest event verified in this case study.
summary: Federal-land AI development moved through policy changes and project negotiations; a November 2026 oversight request asks how BLM is assessing proposals. These events share a theme but are not one project or a proven causal chain.

timeline.title: Federal infrastructure plan
timeline.text: Executive Order 14141 set out a plan for developing AI infrastructure on federal sites. This is historical policy, not evidence that any particular facility was built.
timeline.connection: Starting point for comparing later approaches to federal land and AI infrastructure.

timeline.title: DOE seeks industry input
timeline.text: DOE published an information request about AI infrastructure on its lands, including development approaches and energy needs. An information request does not award a lease.
timeline.connection: A concrete intake step for the federal-land development theme; not a construction milestone.

timeline.title: Permitting policy changes
timeline.text: Executive Order 14318 prioritised facilitating data-centre infrastructure and expressly revoked Executive Order 14141.
timeline.connection: A policy change, so the January order must not be described as the unchanged current framework.

timeline.title: Savannah River negotiations announced
timeline.text: NNSA selected Amentum to enter phased-lease negotiations for a proposed AI data centre and on-site energy project at Savannah River. NNSA explicitly said selection was not a final lease award.
timeline.connection: Illustrates project-level implementation; DOE-site negotiations and BLM land decisions involve different agencies and authorities.

timeline.title: Senate oversight request
timeline.text: Senator Heinrich requested BLM information on legal authorities, proposals and eligible lands for data-centre development, with a requested response date of 20 November 2026.
timeline.connection: Shows an oversight question within the broader federal-land story. The letter establishes the request, not the truth of every allegation or the agency response.

facts.text: Senator Heinrich requested BLM information on legal authorities, proposals and eligible lands for data-centre development, with a requested response date of 20 November 2026.
NNSA announced negotiations, not a final Savannah River lease award.

history.text: The policy framework changed between January and July 2025.
history.comparison: Both orders address AI infrastructure; the later order expressly revoked the earlier one.
history.limitations: A policy statement is not proof of project completion or a common legal basis for every federal site.

scenarios.text: a published agency response could clarify the authorities and review process being used.
scenarios.condition: BLM or the Senate publishes a response to the request
scenarios.signal: an official agency response or committee publication
scenarios.timeframe: The next published response; timing is not established by this case study.

gaps: No agency response to the 20 November request has been verified in this case study as of the research check. This does not establish that no response exists.
The latest verified event here is 6 November 2026; the research-check time is not a newer news event.
This is a selected-source timeline, not an exhaustive archive or a legal assessment.
Project operational status after the cited negotiation announcement has not been verified.
